thread:
Clare: Auditor in the SOC2 call wants the KMS rotation timeline + proof that the RBAC changes for key usage were applied atomically. They asked for a playbook and the exact queries to pull logs. Can someone drop what we usually hand over?
Mike: I can. High level: rotation artifacts + CloudTrail + IAM change events.
Anya: For RBAC changes we have the PRs and the k8s RoleBindings update in git. PRs: #4896 and #4901. Those link to the deploy that updated the key access role.
Leo: Note: there was also a hotfix on 2024-11-12 for the keypolicy; that produced a separate rotation event. Include INC-2024-137 and the vuln triage notes.
Clare: Good — auditor asked for mapping to control: they want to see evidence for 'key lifecycle and access control' (SOC2 CC6.2 / ISO A.8.3 equivalent). Can we annotate artifacts with control IDs?
Mike: Yes. Our evidence set should include: 1) KMS key metadata snapshot, 2) CloudTrail events for kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion / kms:DisableKeyRotation / kms:EnableKeyRotation / kms:RotateKey, 3) IAM/RoleBinding audit events, 4) PRs and deploy logs, 5) incident ticket and triage notes.
Anya: Commands I use to pull logs quickly:
```bash
# CloudTrail lookup for key id
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-1234

# S3 query of exported logs (if needed)
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-cloudtrail-logs/2024/11/12/ ./ --recursive --exclude '*' --include '*kms*'
```
Mike: For GCP customers we export to BigQuery; sample query:
```sql
SELECT protopayload_auditlog.methodName, timestamp, authenticationInfo.principalEmail
FROM `project.dataset.cloudaudit_googleapis_com_activity_*`
WHERE protoPayload.serviceName = 'cloudkms.googleapis.com'
AND timestamp BETWEEN '2024-11-12T00:00:00Z' AND '2024-11-12T23:59:59Z'
```
Clare: Nice. Auditor also asked: how do we prove rotation actually changed the encryption key used for customer artifacts?
Leo: We keep a key-version manifest in the artifact registry. Example entry: `artifact: service-config-2024-11-12, key_id: abcd-1234, key_version: v2`. Include the manifest export and the S3 object HEAD which shows the server-side encryption header.
Anya: Example curl to capture encryption headers from S3 object: `curl -I https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-bucket/path/to/artifact | grep -i x-amz-server-side-encryption`.
AuditBot: Automated note: evidence bundle generator started for rotation 2024-11-12. Bundle id: eb-20241112-77. Upload path: s3://redwood-evidence/eb-20241112-77/ (will contain: cloudtrail.json, key-meta.json, rolebinding-diff.json, prs.json, incident-137.json)
Clare: Perfect. Can we also show that the RBAC change was reviewed and approved? Need reviewer and timestamp.
Mike: PR #4896 shows approvals in the GitHub Checks — approver: @leo, timestamp: 2024-11-11T19:04:21Z. I'll export the PR review json.
Leo: I added a short note in INC-2024-137 about verification steps and a screenshot of the acceptance test.
Clare: Auditor asked for proof that logs haven't been tampered with — any immutable export?
Mike: We export CloudTrail to a dedicated S3 account with object lock enabled and also ship to the log-archive Glacier vault. Evidence: s3://redwood-logs-archive/cloudtrail/ and snapshot job id 2024-11-13-arch-91.
Anya: For RBAC, we can also provide the k8s audit-log snippet that shows the RoleBinding change and the user that applied it. Example snippet:
```json
{"kind":"Event","level":"Request","timestamp":"2024-11-11T19:03:12Z","user":"leo@redwood.com","verb":"update","object":"rolebinding/redwood-key-users"}
```
Clare: Good. Auditor also pressed on 'how quickly can you detect and respond to a suspected key compromise' — they want the IR timeline and SLA.
Leo: Our playbook says: 1) detect (alert within 15m via guardrails), 2) isolate key (rotate or disable within 30m), 3) notify stakeholders within 1 hour, 4) full post-incident review within 7 days. Add the incident timeline from INC-2024-137 to demonstrate.
Clare: Can someone assemble a short README that maps each artifact to a control statement? They want a spreadsheet mapping artifact -> control id -> short note.
Mike: I'll create mapping.csv and upload to the evidence bundle. Sample rows: `cloudtrail.json, SOC2 CC6.2, shows rotation events and actor`, `key-meta.json, SOC2 CC6.2, shows key rotation config & date`.
Anya: Also include the quantized audit sample: we usually pull a 90-day window containing 3 rotation events for the key. I'll export that to cloudtrail-90d.json.
Clare: Thanks. Final ask from auditor: a single signed manifest (SHA256) of the bundle and a short verification recipe. Can we sign with our build key?
Mike: Yes — I'll sign the tar using our KMS-signed detached signature process and include `bundle.sig`. Command: `gpg --output bundle.sig --detach-sign --local-user compliance@redwood.com bundle.tar.gz` (we keep the private key in HSM with access restricted to the compliance role).
AuditBot: Evidence bundle eb-20241112-77 uploaded: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-evidence/eb-20241112-77?region=us-west-2
Clare: Awesome — please put the mapping.csv + bundle.sig + README.md in that bucket and ping the auditor after upload. I'll compile the control mapping sheet and send to them. :thumbsup:
Mike: On it. ETA 30m.
Leo: I'll attach the incident triage doc and screenshots to the bundle.
Anya: Uploading PR exports now.
Clare: Thanks team — this should close the auditor questions for that control. If anything else comes up I'll start a new thread.
